---
title: "Topics"
description: "Questions that the course answers from several angles on different days, each compared side by side on one page."
---

Some questions come up on many days of the course, each time from another angle. A **topic page**
explains the question in plain language, compares the approaches side by side (what each one
assumes, what it costs, when it fails) and links to the units and demos where each is taught.
Use a topic page as a map: to see how methods you have met relate to each other, or to choose the
units you need for one question.

- [Finding points](point-detection.qmd): spots, blobs, correlation peaks, Hough votes and keypoints:
  filter, take local maxima, threshold from the noise, refine to sub-pixel, evaluate.
- [Removing noise](denoising.qmd): averaging, robust and edge-preserving filters, energies with
  priors, sparsity, learned and generative denoisers, and what may be measured afterwards.
- [Eigenvectors in image analysis](eigenvectors.qmd): PCA, the structure tensor, the Hessian, moments,
  shape models, normalized cuts and camera calibration as one question: along which directions is
  something most and least stretched?
- [Energy minimisation](energy.qmd): data + λ · prior, from deconvolution and smoothing to graph
  cuts, snakes, level sets and shortest paths: what each scores, how it searches, and when the best
  score is the wrong answer.
- [Segmentation](segmentation.qmd): thresholds, watersheds, graph methods, energies, moving
  boundaries and learned models on one image: which pixels belong to which object, what each
  method assumes, and how each one fails.
- [Registration and alignment](registration.qmd): shifts, rigid and affine maps, homographies,
  spline deformations and flow; intensities versus features; trying everything, closed forms,
  RANSAC and downhill search.
